title.en: Collaboration, Interpersonal Communication, and Business Etiquette
title.ms: Kolaborasi, Komunikasi Interpersonal dan Etiket Perniagaan

en: List the advantages and disadvantages of teams, characteristics of effective teams, and four key issues of group dynamics
Offer guidelines for collaborative communication, identify collaboration technologies, and give constructive feedback
List the key steps for productive team meetings
Identify the major technologies that enhance or replace in-person meetings
Identify modes of listening, describe the listening process, and explain selective listening
Explain the importance of nonverbal communication and identify six categories of nonverbal expression
Explain the importance of business etiquette and identify key areas where it is essential
ms: Senaraikan kelebihan dan kekurangan pasukan, ciri pasukan berkesan, dan empat isu dinamik kumpulan
Beri garis panduan komunikasi kolaboratif, kenal pasti teknologi kolaborasi, dan beri maklum balas membina
Senaraikan langkah utama mesyuarat pasukan yang produktif
Kenal pasti teknologi utama yang menambah atau menggantikan mesyuarat bersemuka
Kenal pasti mod mendengar, huraikan proses mendengar, dan terangkan pendengaran terpilih
Terangkan kepentingan komunikasi bukan lisan dan kenal pasti enam kategori ekspresi bukan lisan
Terangkan kepentingan etiket perniagaan dan kenal pasti bidang utama yang memerlukannya

en: **Collaboration** = working together to solve complex problems; an essential skill in nearly every profession.
Team members share a mission and are **collectively responsible** for their work.
ms: **Kolaborasi** = bekerjasama menyelesaikan masalah kompleks; kemahiran penting hampir semua profesion.
Ahli pasukan berkongsi misi dan **bertanggungjawab secara kolektif**.

blocks.en: A **team** is a unit of **two or more people** who share a **mission** and the **responsibility** for working to achieve a **common goal**.
blocks.ms: **Pasukan** ialah unit **dua orang atau lebih** yang berkongsi **misi** dan **tanggungjawab** untuk mencapai **matlamat bersama**.

en: Assembles to resolve specific issues; cross-functional for maximum diversity; disbands once goal is achieved
ms: Berhimpun menyelesaikan isu khusus; merentas fungsi untuk kepelbagaian maksimum; bubar bila matlamat dicapai

en: Assembles to resolve specific issues; cross-functional; disbands once goal is achieved
ms: Berhimpun menyelesaikan isu khusus; merentas fungsi; bubar bila matlamat dicapai

en: Assembles regularly for ongoing and recurring issues; focused teams (e.g. strategic planning); formal teams with long life span
ms: Berhimpun secara tetap untuk isu berterusan dan berulang; pasukan fokus (cth perancangan strategik); pasukan formal berjangka hayat panjang

blocks.en: The slide text groups the three columns in a table; I mapped the lines to each team type by reading order. Check slide 5 if unsure.
blocks.ms: Teks slaid mengumpulkan tiga lajur dalam jadual; saya padankan baris kepada setiap jenis mengikut susunan bacaan. Semak slaid 5 jika ragu.

blocks.en: Task force and problem-solving team end when the goal is done. A committee is long-lived.
blocks.ms: Task force dan pasukan penyelesaian masalah tamat bila matlamat siap. Jawatankuasa berpanjangan.

blocks.en: Effective teams pool knowledge, use diverse viewpoints, increase acceptance of solutions and achieve higher performance. They can improve productivity, creativity, employee involvement and even job security, and sit at the core of **participative management** (involving employees in decisions).
blocks.ms: Pasukan berkesan menghimpun pengetahuan, memanfaat pandangan pelbagai, meningkatkan penerimaan penyelesaian dan prestasi. Ia teras **pengurusan penyertaan**.

en: **Information and knowledge**: pooling experience gives access to more information.
**Diverse views**: varied perspectives, as long as guided by a shared goal.
**Acceptance**: people who take part in a decision are more likely to support it.
**Higher performance**: creativity and energy from shared purpose and mutual accountability; effective teams can beat top individuals on complex problems.
ms: **Maklumat dan pengetahuan**: menghimpun pengalaman memberi lebih maklumat.
**Prestasi tinggi**: kreativiti dan tenaga daripada tujuan bersama.

en: **Groupthink**: pressure to conform makes members withhold contrary opinions; teams oversimplify problems, ignore threatening information and fail to consider risks.
**Hidden agenda**: private counterproductive motive (control the group, undermine someone, pursue a goal against the team’s mission).
**Cost**: aligning schedules, meetings and coordination eat time and money.
**Overload**: best contributors get invited to even more teams; individual work is pushed to nights and weekends, causing exhaustion and lower productivity.
ms: **Groupthink**: tekanan mematuhi menyebabkan ahli menyimpan pendapat berbeza; masalah dipermudah dan risiko diabaikan.
**Agenda tersembunyi**: motif peribadi menjejaskan (kawal kumpulan, menjatuhkan orang).
**Kos**: menyelaras jadual, mesyuarat dan kerja memakan masa dan wang.
**Beban berlebihan**: penyumbang terbaik dijemput ke lebih banyak pasukan; kerja individu ditolak ke malam/hujung minggu.

blocks.en: Why teams become dysfunctional: unclear or unaccepted management expectations; reluctance to put team goals before personal goals; reward systems that ignore team contributions; leadership that tolerates negative behaviour.
blocks.ms: Punca pasukan tidak berfungsi: jangkaan pengurusan tidak jelas; enggan utamakan matlamat pasukan; sistem ganjaran abaikan sumbangan pasukan; kepimpinan membiarkan tingkah laku negatif.

en: **Group dynamics** = interactions and processes within a team. Productive teams develop clear **norms** (informal standards of conduct).

Self-oriented members fulfil personal needs and are less productive. “Dream teams” of superstars often underperform because stars struggle to put the team first; difficult personalities may be avoided. Team-maintenance and task-oriented roles contribute most.
**Tuckman’s phases**: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning. Teams may move back and forth, or be productive immediately even while in conflict.
**Causes of conflict**: competition for resources, disagreement over goals or responsibilities, poor communication, power struggles, differences in values, attitudes and personalities.
Conflict is **constructive** if it brings issues into the open, increases involvement and generates creative ideas; **destructive** if it diverts energy, destroys morale or polarises the team.
ms: **Dinamik kumpulan** = interaksi dan proses dalam pasukan. Pasukan produktif ada **norma** jelas (piawaian tidak formal).
Ahli berorientasi diri kurang produktif. “Dream team” bintang sering kurang berprestasi. Peranan penyelenggaraan dan tugas menyumbang paling banyak.
**Fasa Tuckman**: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning. Pasukan boleh bergerak ke depan dan belakang.
**Punca konflik**: persaingan sumber, percanggahan matlamat/tanggungjawab, komunikasi lemah, perebutan kuasa, perbezaan nilai.
Konflik **membina** jika membawa isu terbuka dan idea kreatif; **memusnah** jika mengalih tenaga, merosakkan moral atau memecahbelahkan.

en: Initiating (starts inquiry); Information giving or seeking; Coordinating (shows relationships, summarises); Procedure setting (suggests decision procedures)
ms: Initiating (mulakan siasatan); Memberi/mencari maklumat; Coordinating (tunjuk hubungan, ringkaskan); Procedure setting (cadang prosedur keputusan)

en: Encouraging (support, praise); Harmonizing (mediate, humour); Compromising (yield on a point)
Controlling (dominating); Withdrawing (silent or refuses); Attention seeking; Diverting (topics of personal interest)
ms: Controlling (mendominasi); Withdrawing (diam/enggan); Attention seeking (mahu perhatian); Diverting (topik minat sendiri)

blocks.en: Slide 11 (Allowing for Team Evolution) is an image/figure with no text. The textbook shows the stages of team development.
blocks.ms: Slaid 11 (Allowing for Team Evolution) ialah imej tanpa teks. Buku teks menunjukkan peringkat pembangunan pasukan.

en: Proactive behaviour — Deal with minor conflict before it becomes major.
Communication — Involve those directly affected; choose words and gestures carefully.
Openness — Get feelings out before the main issues.
Research — Seek factual reasons before solutions.
Flexibility — Don’t lock into a position.
Fair play — Insist on fair outcomes; no hiding behind rules.
Alliance — Unite opponents against an “outside force”.
ms: Tingkah laku proaktif — Tangani konflik kecil sebelum membesar.
Komunikasi — Libatkan yang terlibat; pilih kata dan isyarat.
Penyelidikan — Cari sebab fakta sebelum penyelesaian.
Fleksibiliti — Jangan terkunci pada satu pendirian.
Pakatan — Satukan pihak bertentangan menentang “kuasa luar”.

blocks.en: **Resistance to change** can be irrational (resisting any change) or logical (giving up authority or comfortable ways). Overcome it by actively listening, expressing interest, asking questions and moving toward resolution via collaboration.
blocks.ms: **Penentangan terhadap perubahan** boleh tidak rasional atau logik (kehilangan kuasa/cara selesa). Atasi dengan mendengar aktif, tunjuk minat, bertanya dan bergerak ke arah resolusi.

en: Give the team time to bond
Ensure tools are ready and compatible
Think through your suggested changes carefully
Highlight any limitations your feedback may have
ms: Fokus pada tingkah laku yang boleh dikawal
Pilih masa maklum balas dengan teliti

blocks.en: Team collaboration can produce results beyond what individuals do alone, but needs special effort and planning. Members must be flexible and open, focusing on team objectives and avoiding a “my way is best” attitude.
blocks.ms: Kolaborasi boleh menghasilkan lebih daripada kerja individu tetapi perlukan usaha dan perancangan. Ahli mesti fleksibel dan elak sikap “cara saya terbaik”.

en: Select collaborators carefully — For combined experience, information and talent.
Agree on project goals — Before starting (otherwise frustration and wasted time).
Give the team time to bond — Before diving in.
Establish clear processes — From start to finish.

**Avoid composing as a group** — Plan, research and outline together, then assign writing to one person or split it; have one person do the final revision for consistent style. (Short texts such as slogans can be brainstormed.)
Ensure tools are ready and compatible — (even software versions can delay).
Check group progress — Along the way; no news is not good news.
ms: Pilih kolaborator dengan teliti — Untuk gabungan pengalaman, maklumat dan bakat.
Beri masa pasukan mesra — **Beri masa berkenalan**.
**Elak mengarang sebagai kumpulan** — Rancang, kaji dan buat rangka bersama, kemudian satu orang menulis atau bahagikan; satu orang semak akhir.
Pastikan alat sedia dan serasi — **Pastikan alat serasi**.
Semak kemajuan kumpulan — ; tiada aduan tidak bermakna semuanya baik.

en: Simple software tools — Commenting (notes without changing text), tracking changes (separate, reversible edits), Adobe Acrobat PDF group review.
Content management systems — Organise and control website content and help teams work on pages.
Shared online workspaces — = virtual offices; **intranets** (employees only) and **extranets** (employees plus invited outsiders).
Social networks and virtual communities — Erase geographic and organisational boundaries.
Collaboration on mobile devices — Apps support nearly all features of computer platforms; linked to **unified communication**.
ms: Alat perisian ringkas — Komen, jejak perubahan, semakan PDF Acrobat.
Sistem pengurusan kandungan — Mengurus kandungan web dan membantu kerja pasukan.
Ruang kerja dalam talian dikongsi — = pejabat maya; **intranet** (pekerja sahaja) dan **extranet** (pekerja dan pihak luar dijemput).
Rangkaian sosial dan komuniti maya — Menghapus sempadan geografi.
Kolaborasi pada peranti mudah alih — Menyokong hampir semua ciri komputer; dikaitkan dengan **komunikasi bersepadu**.

blocks.en: Say “here is how to make it clearer”, not “this is confusing”. Comment on the message, not the person.
blocks.ms: Cakap “beginilah cara menjadikannya lebih jelas”, bukan “ini mengelirukan”. Komen mesej, bukan orang.

blocks.en: Feedback: be constructive by focusing on how material can be improved. When receiving feedback, keep your emotions in check and view it as a chance to improve.
blocks.ms: Maklum balas: fokus cara menambah baik. Apabila menerima, kawal emosi dan anggap peluang memperbaiki.

ms: Guna peranti mudah alih dengan hormat

en: Be aware of limitations of technology

blocks.en: Well-run meetings solve problems, develop ideas, find opportunities and promote team building. Prepare carefully, conduct efficiently and use meeting technology wisely.
blocks.ms: Mesyuarat baik menyelesaikan masalah, membangun idea, mencari peluang dan membina pasukan.

en: Define your purpose — Exchange information, reach decisions, or collaborate; define the best possible result.
Select participants — Invite everyone who really needs to be there and no one else; more than 10 or 12 becomes unmanageable.
Choose time and venue — Online for multiple locations; check seating, temperature, lighting, ventilation, acoustics, refreshments; mornings are often more productive.
Set the agenda — Answers: What must we do to meet goals? What issues matter most to all? What information is needed? Use a detailed planning agenda, then a simple display agenda with time limits.
ms: Tentukan tujuan — Bertukar maklumat, membuat keputusan atau berkolaborasi.
Pilih peserta — Jemput yang perlu sahaja; lebih 10–12 sukar diurus.
Pilih masa dan tempat — Dalam talian untuk lokasi berbeza; semak tempat duduk, suhu, cahaya; pagi lebih produktif.
Tetapkan agenda — Menjawab: apa perlu dibuat? isu paling penting? maklumat diperlukan? Guna agenda perancangan terperinci, kemudian agenda paparan ringkas bermasa.

en: Keep the discussion on track — Guide, mediate, probe, stimulate, summarise, redirect.
Follow agreed-on rules — Follow agreed rules; formal meetings use **parliamentary procedure** (*Robert’s Rules of Order*); larger meetings need more formality.
Encourage participation — Draw out quiet members; tell talkative ones time is limited.
Participate actively — But don’t talk just to show knowledge.
Use mobile devices respectfully — (notes, tweeting key points = fine; Facebook = not).
Close effectively — Verify objectives, summarise conclusions and actions, clear up misunderstandings.
ms: Pastikan perbincangan kekal fokus — Pastikan perbincangan fokus.
Ikut peraturan dipersetujui — Ikut peraturan; mesyuarat formal guna **prosedur parlimen** (*Robert’s Rules of Order*).
Sertai secara aktif — Sertai aktif tetapi jangan bercakap sekadar menunjuk pandai.
Guna peranti mudah alih dengan hormat — Guna peranti dengan hormat.
Tutup dengan berkesan — Sahkan objektif, ringkaskan tindakan.

en: Include: instant messaging, teleconferencing, telepresence, webinars — IM and teleconferencing (simplest); videoconferencing; **telepresence** (realistic, conveys facial expressions and gestures, good for negotiation and complex discussion); web-based systems with virtual whiteboards; webinars; online brainstorming (“idea campaigns”).
ms: Termasuk: pesanan segera, telesidang, telepresence, webinar — IM, telesidang, sidang video, **telepresence**, sistem web dengan papan putih maya, webinar, sumbang saran dalam talian.

en: Extra planning — Successful virtual meetings need **extra planning**, awareness of limits (less nonverbal contact), keeping people engaged, background material sent beforehand so time is for discussion, and chances to participate.
Be aware of limitations of technology
ms: Perancangan tambahan — Mesyuarat maya perlukan **perancangan tambahan**, kesedaran had teknologi, penglibatan, bahan latar dihantar awal.

blocks.ms: Slaid 24 dan 25 (Agenda Mesyuarat; Merekod Keputusan) ialah rajah tanpa teks.

en: **Minutes** = written summary of important information and decisions; record responsibilities assigned; software can forward action items and store audio and documents (Figure 2.5).
ms: **Minit** = ringkasan bertulis maklumat dan keputusan; rekod tanggungjawab; perisian boleh hantar tindakan.

groups.en: Five steps of the listening process

en: About **80%** of top executives say listening is the most important skill for getting things done. Poor listening costs companies millions through lost opportunities and legal mistakes.
ms: Kira-kira **80%** eksekutif kata mendengar ialah kemahiran terpenting. Pendengaran lemah merugikan berjuta.

en: **Content listening** — Understand and retain information; don’t evaluate; overlook style.
**Critical listening** — Evaluate logic, evidence, validity, implications, motives and omissions; separate fact from opinion; watch for bias.
**Empathic listening** — Understand the speaker’s feelings, needs and wants; helps the person vent emotions.
**Active listening** — Turn off your own filters and biases; ask questions to verify; show positive body language.
ms: **Mendengar kandungan** — Faham dan ingat; tidak menilai.
**Mendengar kritis** — Nilai logik, bukti, motif, kecuaian; bezakan fakta dan pendapat.
**Mendengar empati** — Faham perasaan dan keperluan penutur.
**Mendengar aktif** — Matikan penapis dan bias; tanya untuk sahkan.

blocks.en: The learning objective says three major modes; the slide lists four terms. Your textbook treats content, critical and empathic as the three modes and active listening as a technique. Confirm with your lecturer.
blocks.ms: Objektif kata tiga mod utama; slaid menyenaraikan empat istilah. Buku teks menganggap content, critical dan empathic sebagai tiga mod dan active listening sebagai teknik. Sahkan dengan pensyarah.

ms: Tiada nota atau nota tidak berkesan
Kurang atau tidak sesuai pandang mata

en: Adjust listening style to the situation
Overlook style differences, focus on message
ms: Abaikan beza gaya, fokus pada mesej

blocks.en: Selective listening (LO 2.5) is not explained in the slide text. Extra (not in slides): it means hearing only what you want to hear. Check your textbook.
blocks.ms: Pendengaran terpilih (LO 2.5) tidak dijelaskan dalam teks slaid. Extra (bukan dalam slaid): bermaksud hanya mendengar apa yang anda mahu dengar. Semak buku teks.

blocks.en: Five steps of the listening process

en: **Receiving**: physically hearing and acknowledging; blocked by noise, impaired hearing or inattention.
**Decoding**: assigning meaning using values, beliefs, expectations and nonverbal signals (e.g. sarcasm: “Well, that’s just lovely”).
**Evaluating**: critical thinking; separate fact from opinion; assess evidence.
**Responding**: verbal feedback one-on-one; applause, laughter or silence in an audience; later action.
ms: **Menerima**: mendengar dan mengakui; terhalang oleh bunyi atau kurang perhatian.
**Menyahkod**: memberi makna ikut nilai, kepercayaan dan isyarat bukan lisan (cth sindiran).
**Bertindak balas**: maklum balas lisan; tepukan, ketawa atau senyap; kemudian tindakan.

en: Some factors (acoustics, poor phone reception) are outside your control; others you can control (don’t interrupt, don’t create distractions). Texting or checking your watch also interrupts the speaker.
**Selective listening**: mind wanders, then you recall what you think the speaker probably said.
**Defensive listening**: protecting the ego by tuning out what doesn’t confirm your beliefs; deciding before the speaker finishes.
ms: Sesetengah faktor di luar kawalan; yang lain boleh dikawal. Menghantar teks atau melihat jam juga mengganggu penutur.
**Mendengar terpilih**: fikiran melayang, kemudian anda ingat apa yang disangka.
**Mendengar defensif**: melindungi ego dengan mengabaikan apa yang tidak sepadan kepercayaan.

groups.ms: Guna komunikasi bukan lisan dengan berkesan

blocks.en: Nonverbal communication can supplement or even replace verbal messages.
blocks.ms: Komunikasi bukan lisan boleh menambah atau menggantikan mesej lisan.

blocks.en: Make nonverbal signals match your spoken tone and content. When talking, be aware of cues you send; when not talking, clothes, posture and walk still communicate; when listening, watch the speaker’s cues and ask an honest, respectful question if something feels wrong.
blocks.ms: Pastikan isyarat sepadan dengan kata-kata. Semasa bercakap, tidak bercakap dan mendengar, perhatikan isyarat.

en: Facial expression — Primary vehicle for emotion (type and intensity); eyes show attention and interest, influence, regulate interaction and establish dominance.
Gesture and posture — Voluntary and involuntary messages; a wave has a specific meaning.
Vocal characteristics — Intentional and unintentional messages; control pitch, pace and stress.
Personal appearance — People respond to physical appearance, sometimes unfairly.
Touch — Warmth, comfort, reassurance and control; governed by cultural customs. When in doubt, don’t touch.
Time and space — Assert authority or imply intimacy; expectations vary by culture.
ms: Ekspresi muka — Wahana utama emosi; mata menunjukkan perhatian dan dominasi.
Gerak isyarat dan postur — Mesej sukarela dan tidak sukarela.
Ciri vokal — Kawal nada, rentak dan tekanan.
Penampilan peribadi — Orang bertindak balas pada penampilan, kadang tidak adil.
Sentuhan — Kemesraan dan kawalan; ikut budaya. Jika ragu, jangan sentuh.
Masa dan ruang — Tunjuk kuasa atau keakraban; berbeza mengikut budaya.

blocks.ms: Guna komunikasi bukan lisan dengan berkesan

blocks.ms: Cara ingat: F-G-V-P-T-T (Face, Gesture, Voice, Personal look, Touch, Time/space).

End calls with courtesy and clarity
Use your outgoing voicemail message to help callers
Be considerate and clear when leaving voicemail

Guna mesej peti suara untuk bantu pemanggil
Bertimbang rasa dan jelas bila tinggalkan peti suara

en: Representing your company; observing dining etiquette
Use virus protection and secure passwords
Avoid profanity and emoticons; avoid multitasking
Don’t waste others’ time with sloppy messages
Be careful of online commenting mechanisms
ms: Guna perlindungan virus dan kata laluan selamat
Elak carutan dan emotikon; elak multitugas
Jangan bazirkan masa orang dengan mesej cuai

en: Be aware of expectations and policies
ms: Amalkan tabiat penggunaan peribadi yang baik

en: Etiquette is part of every aspect of business communication. Be aware of your effect on others, treat everyone with respect, remember the lasting impression. “Respect, consideration and honesty are universal and timeless” (Cindy Post Senning).
ms: Etiket ialah sebahagian setiap aspek komunikasi. Sedar kesan anda, hormati semua orang. “Hormat, pertimbangan dan kejujuran sejagat dan abadi.”

en: Personal appearance — Match the dress style where you work; grooming matters; avoid strong scents (perfume, cologne, aftershave) because some people are allergic; phone skills remain essential even with IM.
ms: Penampilan peribadi — Padankan gaya pakaian; kekemasan penting; elak wangian kuat; kemahiran telefon tetap penting.

en: Be conscious of how your voice sounds — Vary your pitch (avoid monotone); slow down for non-native speakers.
Be courteous — Identify yourself and organisation, state the reason, check it is a good time, plan important calls.
Convey a positive, professional attitude — Promptly, with a smile, identify yourself and company, ask “How may I help you?”
End calls with courtesy and clarity — End with courtesy and clarity; double-check vital details.
Use your outgoing voicemail message to help callers — Brief professional outgoing voicemail; when leaving voicemail give name, number, reason and times reachable; speak slowly.
Be considerate and clear when leaving voicemail
ms: Sedar bunyi suara anda — Variasi nada; perlahan untuk bukan penutur asli.
Bersopan — Kenal diri, nyatakan sebab, tanya masa sesuai.
Tunjuk sikap positif dan profesional — Segera, senyum, kenal diri, tanya “How may I help you?”
Tamat panggilan dengan sopan dan jelas — Tamat dengan sopan; semak butiran penting.
Guna mesej peti suara untuk bantu pemanggil — Mesej peti suara ringkas; tinggalkan nama, nombor, sebab dan masa; cakap perlahan.
Bertimbang rasa dan jelas bila tinggalkan peti suara

en: Meeting others: introduce yourself, introduce others, observe customs (especially international business)
Business meals: choose foods that are easy to eat, avoid alcohol, choose appropriate conversation topics
Representing your company; observing dining etiquette
ms: Berjumpa orang: perkenal diri, perkenal orang lain, patuhi adat (terutama perniagaan antarabangsa)
Jamuan perniagaan: pilih makanan mudah dimakan, elak alkohol, pilih topik sesuai

en: Avoid personal attacks; stay on topic; don’t present opinions as facts — Avoid personal attacks; stay on topic (start a new message for a new subject); don’t present opinions as facts.
Follow correct grammar and spelling — Follow spelling, punctuation and capitalisation; use up-to-date virus protection and secure passwords.
Use virus protection and secure passwords
Ask if it is a good time to IM chat — Ask if it is a good time for an IM chat; watch your language; avoid multitasking; **never assume privacy** (everything may be stored forever and forwarded).
Avoid profanity and emoticons; avoid multitasking

Do NOT use “Reply All” unnecessarily — Don’t use **Reply All** unless everyone benefits; don’t send sloppy or confusing messages; respect boundaries of time and virtual space; be careful with online commenting (Facebook login may reveal job title and company).
Don’t waste others’ time with sloppy messages; respect boundaries
Be careful of online commenting mechanisms
ms: Elak serangan peribadi; kekal pada topik; jangan sampaikan pendapat sebagai fakta — Elak serangan peribadi; kekal topik; jangan nyatakan pendapat sebagai fakta.
Ikut tatabahasa dan ejaan betul — Ikut ejaan dan tanda baca; guna perlindungan virus dan kata laluan selamat.
Guna perlindungan virus dan kata laluan selamat
Tanya sama ada sesuai untuk IM — Tanya jika sesuai untuk IM; jaga bahasa; elak multitugas; **jangan anggap privasi**.
Elak carutan dan emotikon; elak multitugas
JANGAN guna “Reply All” sewenang-wenangnya — Jangan guna **Reply All** kecuali semua mendapat manfaat; hormati sempadan masa dan ruang maya; hati-hati komen dalam talian.
Jangan bazirkan masa orang dengan mesej cuai; hormati sempadan
Berhati-hati dengan mekanisme komen dalam talian

en: Implement good personal use habits — Obnoxious ringtones, loud talk in open offices, excessive personal calls, camera use without permission, calls in restrooms, texting during a meal or while someone speaks, calls interrupting meetings.
Be aware of expectations and policies — Older employees, managers and customers are less tolerant than younger people. Virtual assistants (e.g. Siri) can distract and annoy others.
